For SSH the keys of the running ssh-agent (Pageant on Windows) are used instead of a key file and a password.
User is the key of an API key, password its secret: System → Access → Users → API keys in OPNsense
pfSense answers through the package pfSense-pkg-RESTAPI v2. Leave the user empty and give a key of System → REST API → Keys as the password, or the user and password of its local database.
Keenetic and Netcraze are only read here. Give the user and password of the web interface, or leave the user empty and give an access token of KeeneticOS 5.2 from Users and access as the password.

VyOS 1.4 and later answer through service https api. Leave the user empty and give the key of service https api keys id … key as the password. Each change is committed and saved at once; with Safe Mode on, a change after which the app cannot reach the router is taken back by commit-confirm within a minute.
The password is the community of SNMP v2c; the user is not used. Nothing is written over SNMP.

The user and password are those of an SNMPv3 user; with no password the agent is asked without authentication. In RouterOS the user is the name of an /snmp community, the passwords its authentication-password and encryption-password. Nothing is written over SNMP.
Without a privacy password every value travels unencrypted; the password itself is never sent.

Port 1900 finds the description of the device by SSDP; another port is that of the description, as 49000 of a FRITZ!Box. The user and password are those of TR-064 where the device asks for them. Nothing is written.
Directly, or through the SSH of a saved router when this one cannot be reached from here, as ssh -J does.

Reload the menus and fields from the router

NetworkHelm is a client for routers: one menu tree, windows in a single workspace, tables that update live, item dialogs with tabs, Safe Mode, a terminal and a file browser. It works with MikroTik RouterOS 7 and 6, OpenWrt, OPNsense, pfSense, VyOS, Keenetic and Linux hosts over SSH, and reads devices over SNMP and UPnP. One Kotlin codebase builds for Windows, macOS, Linux, Android, iOS and the browser. The app sends nothing to its developer: no account, no analytics, no crash reports.

The port listens on 127.0.0.1 only; 0 takes a free one. RouterOS forwards only where forwarding-enabled in /ip ssh allows it.

The client opens a TCP connection to each port, reads the greeting of SSH and asks the web server for its first page, without logging in. A router that guards against password guessing may still count that as an attempt and block the address.
